 UFC 334: Gane vs. Hokit features an explosive lightweight preliminary clash between all-time division knockout leader Drew Dober and Scottish finisher Chris Duncan. Check out our UFC 334 odds series for our Dober-Duncan prediction and pick.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Drew Dober (29-15, 1 NC) enters this bout on a two-fight knockout streak after extending his UFC lightweight record to 11 knockouts. Following a third-round TKO win over Kyle Prepolec in October 2025, the 38-year-old veteran starched Michael Johnson in the second round at UFC 326 in March as he comes into his fight this weekend against Chris Duncan.
 Chris Duncan (15-3) looks to rebound after having his four-fight winning streak snapped by Renato Moicano via second-round submission in his April main event slot. Prior to that setback, the Scotsman defeated Mateusz Rebecki by decision and submitted Terrance McKinney in December 2025 as he comes into his fight this weekend against Drew Dober.

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement UFC 334 Odds: Drew Dober-Chris Duncan Odds 
 Drew Dober: +154
 Chris Duncan: -185
 Over 1.5 rounds: -130
 Under 1.5 rounds: +100
 Why Drew Dober Will Win 
 Drew Dober holds the record for the most knockouts in UFC lightweight history with 11, and Chris Duncan's aggressive, hittable style gives Dober every opportunity to make it 12. Fighting out of the southpaw stance, Dober marches forward with a granite chin and throws thunderous left hands and looping hooks to the head and body.
 Duncan loves to engage in wild pocket firefights, as seen in his absolute war with Mateusz Rebecki and his chaotic first-round exchanges with Terrance McKinney. While Duncan survived those battles through sheer toughness, standing in the pocket and trading hooks with Dober is a dangerous proposition for anyone at 155 pounds.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Dober proved in his recent knockouts of Kyle Prepolec and Michael Johnson that he still carries fight-ending power deep into the second and third rounds. Even if he loses the opening frame or absorbs heavy shots early, Dober never stops walking forward and hunting his opponent's chin.
 If Duncan gets drawn into an emotional brawl instead of utilizing his wrestling, Dober's compact southpaw counters will find the mark and produce another highlight-reel knockout.
 Why Chris Duncan Will Win 
 Chris Duncan possesses a clear path to victory by blending his heavy-handed striking with the opportunistic wrestling and submission game that carried him to four straight wins prior to facing Renato Moicano. At 33 years old, Duncan is five years younger than the 38-year-old Drew Dober and has absorbed significantly less career damage.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While fans remember Duncan for his wild brawls, three of his last four victories—over Bolaji Oki, Jordan Vucenic and Terrance McKinney—actually came via guillotine or anaconda choke submissions. Training at American Top Team, "The Problem" has evolved into a well-rounded threat who punishes opponents in transition and on the mat.
 Dober has historically struggled against physical grapplers who can mix takedowns with heavy top control, as Renato Moicano showed when he outwrestled Dober to a decision. Furthermore, Dober was knocked out in the first round by Manuel Torres in early 2025, showing that his legendary chin is no longer completely indestructible at age 38.
 If Duncan mixes in level changes, threatens front chokes and avoids trading reckless hooks in the pocket, he will outwork or submit Dober inside two rounds.
 Final Dober-Duncan Prediction & Pick 
 Chris Duncan is the pick in what should be a lightweight Fight of the Night contender because he brings more paths to victory and superior grappling upside at this stage of their careers. While Drew Dober is always live to land a nuclear left hand, backing a 38-year-old brawler against a physical, well-rounded finisher from American Top Team is risky.
 Click Above to Subscribe Both men love to trade leather, meaning the opening three minutes of this fight will be pure chaos in the center of the Octagon. Dober will look to back Duncan up and unload his signature southpaw combinations, while Duncan will fire back with heavy calf kicks and right hands.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The difference is that Duncan does not have to keep this fight purely on the feet when the exchanges heat up. Over the last two years, Duncan has developed a lethal front-headlock game, choking out Bolaji Oki, Jordan Vucenic and Terrance McKinney whenever scrambles ensue.
 Expect a thrilling first round where both men land heavy leather before Duncan mixes in a timely takedown or catches a hurt Dober shooting in, locking up a guillotine or anaconda choke before the halfway mark.
 Final Drew Dober-Chris Duncan Prediction & Pick: Chris Duncan (-185), UNDER 1.5 rounds (+100)
